title: Deleting an Already-Overridden Single Instance Removes Override and Excludes Master Slot

citations.verbatim_quote: The entries in the "recurrenceOverrides" property convert depending on the contents of the PatchObject value. A PatchObject that sets the "excluded" member to "true" converts to an EXDATE property for the date-time of that recurrence instance. An empty PatchObject converts to an RDATE property. Any other PatchObject converts to a recurrence override component in the embedding VCALENDAR component.

If the patch object defines the "excluded" property of an occurrence to be true, this occurrence is omitted from the final set of recurrences for the calendar object (like an EXDATE from iCalendar). Such a patch object MUST NOT patch any other property.

The final recurrence set is generated by gathering all of the start DATE-TIME values generated by any of the specified "RRULE" and "RDATE" properties, and then excluding any start DATE-TIME values specified by "EXDATE" properties.

rationale: In the JSCalendar/CalExt formal model (RFC 8984 Section 4.3.5 and draft-ietf-calext-jscalendar-icalendar Section 3.2), a recurrence instance at key RECURRENCE-ID maps to a single entry in recurrenceOverrides. When an instance is modified as a single-instance override, that entry is a PatchObject that converts to a standalone override VEVENT/VTODO component with RECURRENCE-ID. When that same instance is subsequently deleted as a single instance, its entry in recurrenceOverrides transitions to `{"excluded": true}` (which MUST NOT patch any other property), which in iCalendar converts to an EXDATE on the master component and NO override component in the VCALENDAR. If the override component were removed without EXDATE being present on the master component, the master's RRULE would regenerate the unedited occurrence.
store_implication: When a single-instance deletion is invoked for a recurrence identifier that currently has a standalone override component, the calendar store MUST: (1) remove the standalone override component from the calendar, AND (2) ensure the recurrence slot (parsed and timezone-aligned to the master component's DTSTART) is present in the master component's EXDATE set (without duplicating it if the master's EXDATE set already contains that timestamp). In timeline expansion, neither the override nor the original master occurrence for that recurrence identifier may appear.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Calendar loaded from an external RFC 5545 iCalendar stream where a single-instance override component (with RECURRENCE-ID) exists WITHOUT a corresponding EXDATE on the master component: deleting that single instance MUST both remove the override component and append the recurrence identifier to the master component's EXDATE list; otherwise removing only the override component causes the original unedited master occurrence to reappear on the timeline.

Calendar where a prior single-instance edit already recorded the recurrence identifier in the master component's EXDATE list: deleting that single instance removes the override component and MUST leave the timestamp in the master's EXDATE list without adding a duplicate EXDATE entry.

scenarios.name: delete_previously_overridden_instance_with_existing_exdate
scenarios.description: Deleting an already-overridden instance where the master already has EXDATE removes the override component while keeping the slot excluded in the master's EXDATE without duplication.

scenarios.name: delete_parsed_override_without_prior_master_exdate
scenarios.description: When an iCalendar object has a master VEVENT (without EXDATE) and a RECURRENCE-ID override VEVENT, deleting that instance with Range=NONE removes the override and adds EXDATE to the master component.
